output.brief: The rejections came from a data error in the new documentation system. When the mandarin product record was set up on 1 Aug, it was copied from avocados and kept the avocado carriage temperature of 7.0°C. The cooperative's specification for mandarins is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through the new system (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was sent at 7.0°C and ran at that setting. All five were rejected. Every container at 4.0°C passed, whichever carrier, fungicide stock or route. Meridane's units did what they were told, so a claim against them would fail. The fungicide, the transit time and Lower Serra fruit don't explain the pattern. Lower Serra fruit may be somewhat more susceptible, but accepted containers weren't surveyed, so that is unproven. Don't suspend growers, switch fungicide or claim against the carrier. Next steps: correct the 7.0°C setting on the mandarin record today. Have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct to 4.0°C. Add a pre-submission check of reefer settings against the product specification. Review how the product record was signed off. I'm confident in this diagnosis. Loggers are a reasonable extra safeguard.
